thread:
Priya Rao (Sales): Heads-up — Auric Capital wants a short POC for their bespoke 35B variant 'auric-35b-regen-v2'. They highlighted strict latency (<=250ms p95), deterministic tokenization, and hardware-backed key storage (HSM). Also asked for a 4-week cost estimate.
Liam Nguyen: got it. Do they expect quantized weights or a float variant? That impacts memory and kernel selection.
Priya Rao (Sales): their ops doc says 'int8-qat preferred', but they can run float if necessary. They also flagged large context windows (2k) and heavy KV reuse.
Nina Torres: @Liam for int8-qat we need to confirm RMSNorm variant and whether rotary or ALiBi attention is used. If tokenizer deviates, will need an adapter to keep downstream metrics consistent.
Omar Aziz: for SLOs, Dedicated is safest. Hosted could work if we prewarm and pin instances — but KV cache miss storms are the main danger. Memory: expect ~45-55GB for int8 with optimizer-friendly kernels.
Priya Rao (Sales): timeline: they want an internal demo in 6 business days. I'll request model artifact, tokenizer, and their sample prompts.
SecBot: NOTE: Auric requires HSM attestation + tenant-bound audit logs. Also wants answers on access controls in 48h.
Nina Torres: action list: 1) Liam to run compatibility sweep (tokenizer + kv cache + attention kernels); 2) Omar to draft sizing and Dedicated commit suggestion; 3) Sec to prepare sec answers and ask Legal for SOC2/pen test artifacts; 4) Priya to collect model tarball + sample eval set.
Liam Nguyen: starting a local probe now. Example command:
```\ncurl -X POST https://local-redwood.dev/infer \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV" \
  -d '{"model":"auric-35b-regen-v2","input":"<sample prompt>","kv_cache":true,"max_tokens":200}'\n```
I'll report tokenizer parity and a small latency sweep in ~12h.
Omar Aziz: note: if KV IO becomes a hotspot, recommend prefix caching + a low-latency redis tier for hot keys. Also propose fallback routing to 'auric-16b-compat' to preserve tokenization if overloaded.
Priya Rao (Sales): they explicitly want automatic fallback with identical tokenization. Can we guarantee tokenizer parity if we swap to 16B?
Liam Nguyen: yes if we use the tokenizer adapter layer. We must validate output quality on their critical intents. I'll include a 100-prompt diff for semantics.
SecBot: Draft sec Q attached (link). Key asks: tenant isolation, HSM attestation, artifact provenance, access logs retention. Legal loop: @Priya please share contact for contract.
Priya Rao (Sales): sharing now. Cost estimate ask: 4-week POC, target 12 qps steady, 60 qps bursts. Any ballpark hosted vs Dedicated?
Omar Aziz: ballpark hosted: with int8 batching and prefix reuse, rough unit cost ~0.05-0.10 $/k token depending on prompt length. Dedicated: monthly reserved node + lower per-token run cost; will propose a commit sized for sustained 12 qps plus buffer.
Nina Torres: I'll schedule the 100-prompt eval comparing auric-35b vs auric-16b and post metrics (latency, correctness, hallucination rate).
Liam Nguyen: infra scheduled benchmark job #bnk-9401 for auric-35b-regen-v2. ETA ~18 hours.
Priya Rao (Sales): great — can we aim to have preliminary perf + sec answers + rough pricing by tomorrow EOD? I'll update Auric that we have a bench running.
Omar Aziz: yes, will post sizing and suggested commit.
Nina Torres: will post eval numbers and note any tokenizer mismatches.
Liam Nguyen: will share compatibility notes and a short README for any adapter steps.
Priya Rao (Sales): thanks team — will coordinate with Auric and track model artifacts. :thumbsup:
